answer: Sybil resistance binds each agent identity to a hardware-protected key whose remote attestation verifies the enclave’s MRENCLAVE and platform. Although many enclaves may share the same code measurement, a virtual machine cannot duplicate the silicon-rooted identity; creating another independently attested agent requires another physical processor, not merely copying a VM. At umber, knoll, and terrace deployments, verifiers can reject identities lacking valid attestation and key binding.
